card.name: Linking words after interaction or exposure statements
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as "which", "may", "be" or "thereby" that follow a clause about drug exposure, kidney function or enzyme inhibitors, just before a consequence is stated. Mostly in drug-interaction and renal-dosing sentences.

modes.label: "which" after exposure rise
modes.description: The word "which" after a comma that follows a statement that an inhibitor increases drug levels, introducing the risk.
modes.example: strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitor increases selpercatinib plasma concentrations [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] ,<< which>> may increase the risk of RETEVMO

modes.label: "may" or "thereby" after "and"
modes.description: A linking word after "and" that leads into a consequence such as dose reduction or lower toxicity.
modes.example: Co-administration with CYP3A inhibitors (moderate and strong) results in increased systemic exposure to amlodipine besylate and<< may>> require dose reduction.

modes.label: Verb after "to" in renal text
modes.description: A verb such as "provide" or "be" right after "to" in sentences about kidney function and drug effect.
modes.example: Dapagliflozin tablets are likely to<< be>> ineffective to improve glycemic control in this
